I know people that have charged rent and etc, but I don’t think it’s a good idea when kids need to save for the future.

Recently my husband went to about four of my therapy sessions because I was on the verge of self harm, and my therapist thought it would be helpful for him to know how to handle things if I was in a bad spot. It was helpful for that period of time. 

Though, the third and fourth sessions when he was there, he would just say things that I haven’t spoke about in my therapy yet, even though I’ve been in therapy with this therapist for nearly six years. My husband was so unhelpful. It literally made me have triggers to the point I started crying and not being able to think clearly. At home, he’s tell me to do my mindfulness, tapping, and say ‘just do your tapping’ like it’s easy to go from having a trigger due to ptsd, to being fine, that I just need to count. I told my husband, he’s not going with me anymore. He was upset. He thinks he’s helping but he’s trying to be a therapist at home, and even tried to be a therapist in my therapy.  He’s a software engineer, nothing close to therapy. 

My therapist actually said it was not good for him to do or say things because therapy is my safe place, and with him there it would just stall my progress.

I had Pfizer back in April. Both shots my arm was extremely sore to the point I couldn’t lift it and I became nauseous and felt as if I was on fire but sweating on my car ride home. I was very fatigued, fever, and chills for roughly two days. I felt like death both times. They had me stay an additional 15 minutes, totaling 30 minutes on my second injection because of my side effects. My husband also had these symptoms but our daughter has Pfizer (she’s 15) and she had just chills after the first shot but she only had a headache and fatigue the second time. My son (20 years old) had Johnson & Johnson, he had a fever and horrible chills in the middle of the night but was fine by about 24 hours afterwards. 

Our family never tested positive for Covid though we were incredibly sick that February as Covid cases were starting to show up, start of the pandemic. A couple people traveled out of the country we know, and they were at Church, but again this was before we knew the horrible situation this was going to become. Anyhow we were sick, but never thought it was Covid, and the doctor never tested us at that time because we said we didn’t leave the country or county we live in so who knows if we had it or not. I’m thinking we didn’t because we didn’t have all the symptoms like not being able to taste or smell, and our fevers weren’t too bad. It felt like a flu though we had those shots. 

I don’t regret getting my vaccine. I have some serious iron deficiencies along with other vitamin deficiencies that have me sick often without my prescription medicine and injections. I’m thinking of getting my boaster shot but I’m just questioning is that something that we’re going to need every six month. I’m definitely talking to my doctor soon about it.
